The operator's published specifications do not include the megawatt capacity, annual power consumption, renewable energy mix, water usage, or cooling architecture for this facility. Without published capacity figures, the role of this specific building in Arizona's data center footprint cannot be quantified from available data.

Arizona has 56 mapped data center facilities, of which only four have published power capacities totaling 512 megawatts. Iron Mountain AZP-2 is not among the four facilities with published megawatt figures. Ranking this campus fifth by published megawatts in the state is therefore impossible; the ranking reflects only the four facilities with disclosed capacity, and AZP-2's actual position relative to others in Arizona remains unknown.

The absence of published specifications for this facility, despite its operation as a hyperscale data center campus, is typical across Arizona's mapped infrastructure. Whether AZP-2 matters to AI scaling depends on its actual capacity and grid connection, neither of which Iron Mountain has disclosed in sources available to this site.
